title: Integrate server-authorized native Case Queue selection with existing Case Workspace handoff
goal: Expose CAP-INV-101 Class-0 Case Queue -> INV-CAS-001 navigation through the native owner-authorized HTTP projection, reusing OpenCaseWorkspace and RestoreCaseQueue without new Case or authorization semantics.
invariants: Existing native Queue session/provider/object authorization remains the only owner of authorization; no client-selected tenant, environment, Saved View, privilege or origin.
OpenCaseWorkspace is the existing first-party transition engine; it reprojects the same authorized candidate graph and refuses denied, filtered, missing or stale Case IDs.
An opaque URL-decoded Case ID remains byte-exact, and ReturnToken is presentation state only. RestoreCaseQueue must recheck current Case/read and view state; never treat the token as authorization.
No new Case mutation, export, incident Task ownership, production IAM or durable queue/provider introduced.
security_properties: HTTP selection is parsed as a single bounded literal; malformed, unexpected or duplicate params and orphaned/invalid scroll fail before session/provider access.
Server filters every Case and independently authorizes Incident/Finding before the first-party selection; denied Case IDs/titles never returned.
Stale Cases and Cases filtered out by the current query are not eligible for navigation, including existing token return state.
Preserve no-store, no-referrer, authorization vary, response caps and generic errors.

migration.rationale: Read-only navigation response only; no migration, IAM or storage change.

rollback.strategy: Revert optional HTTP open_case/scroll branch; preserve existing native Queue listing/filter/sort and all first-party handoff semantics.
verification: Original GET projection and all prior tests remain unchanged
No stored Case, token, Saved View or authorization changes

inputs: E10-INV-101F verified read-only Case Queue projection and E10-INV-101D-HANDOFF verified canonical first-party OpenCaseWorkspace/RestoreCaseQueue engine.
E10-INV-101I-FILTERS implemented native HTTP filter/sort on frozen parent SHA 030b06748d0c0d646e3f95b1e67e12631e73321b with engineering-kernel run 39253620402 SUCCESS (not accepted; L2 pending).
outputs: Native Class-0 GET Case selection returns the existing WorkspaceHandoff for precisely one currently owner-authorized filter-visible non-stale Case.
Behavioral Go HTTP tests prove authorized navigation/restoration, denied/stale/filtered response fail-closed and early invalid query rejection.
acceptance_tests: Selecting accessible Case from a filtered native Queue preserves exact opaque ID, filters, sort and scroll in the existing handoff return token; RestoreCaseQueue reauthorizes.
Case filtered out, stale, denied or missing cannot return a navigation token; changing current Case permission blocks token restoration.
Unknown, duplicate, malformed, tenant/permission/origin override, invalid scroll rejected before any provider or auth call.
Legacy query-only GET remains a normal authorized projection, with exact-head mandatory security CI and independent review recorded.

performance_budget.rationale: No new data collection. Bounded <=5000 owner candidate list and existing native sorting/projection, with one additional in-memory first-party handoff projection only when opening selected Case.
metrics: Single <=1024-byte opaque Case selection and bounded scroll; <=4096 raw query bytes, <=7 unique keys
No additional provider or owner authorization pass after original full server ACL scan
One extra bounded in-memory projector pass for selected Case only
